findings.title: Write and state-transition actions gated by `view` permissions (action mismatch)

findings.title: Webhook endpoint and delivery reads are available to any org member (not manage-gated)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:53-70 — GET / has no requirePermission (router-level requireAuth+requireOrgAccess only)

findings.title: API keys store `expires_at` but nothing enforces or prunes expiry
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/api-key.ts:81-83 — authenticateApiKey rejects is_active=false and expires_at <= now (fail-closed)
apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:67-88 — mct_* bearer tokens are routed through authenticateApiKey before the JWT/Supabase paths

apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:17-21 — create schema still accepts an arbitrary expiresAt (or none)
findings.impact: The indefinite-credential-validity risk is closed: expired and revoked keys are rejected at authentication. Residual: expired/inactive rows accumulate (no pruner), and keys without an expiry remain valid forever unless manually revoked.
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled pruner (or an index/partial cleanup) for expired+inactive api_keys rows and consider defaulting expiresAt in the create schema; document the lifecycle.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: enforcement is present and tested; pruning is absent. Related new finding: key-scoped `permissions` are not enforced.

findings.title: Webhook signing secrets are stored plaintext with no rotation or expiry
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302032_webhook_endpoints.sql:8 — `secret text` column
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:287 (insert), :341 (update) — caller-supplied secret stored as-is; :449-455 HMAC-SHA256 signing; :23-35 masked on read only
grep of supabase/migrations for webhook secret alterations — no later migration encrypts the column or adds expiry/rotation

findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: column still plaintext, no rotation/expiry evidence; file unchanged since 9c0b88c.

findings.title: Profiles are enumerable by email/id for any authenticated user
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:56-91 — GET / accepts ?ids= and ?email=, returns select('*'), no self/role restriction; an unfiltered call returns every profile visible to the caller
apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:93-118 — GET /:id restricts to self or is_super_admin, an intent defeated by the collection endpoint
supabase/migrations/5302026_supabase_consolidated_fresh_bootstrap_20260529.corrected.v3.sql:997-1013 — profiles select policy = self OR is_super_admin OR shared approved membership
apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:58 — the handler uses getSupabaseUser (RLS client), so the query is RLS-scoped: blast radius is same-org, not global

findings.recommendation: Restrict GET / to caller-visible ids (same-org members), drop or gate the ?email= filter behind users:view, and stop returning select('*') (exclude encrypted_pii).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: endpoint unchanged; RLS narrows the finding from 'any authenticated user' to 'any same-org approved member'. File unchanged since 9c0b88c.

findings.title: Client-side permission hiding is UI-only for several module actions

findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: broad server-side enforcement confirmed by route scan (182 requirePermission call sites across 442 route definitions); residual exceptions and missing coverage gate documented.

findings.title: No catalog-lint: referenced permission keys are not checked against the `permissions` table
evidence: grep for permission-catalog tests/scripts (apps/api/src/__tests__, scripts/, .github) — none found
fresh scan at 8d299b8d: 94 distinct requirePermission(module,action) keys across route files; all 94 currently resolve to catalog rows (5302118 + 5302131 + 5302424 + 5302426)
supabase/migrations/5302426_status_actions.sql — records the last real drift (status:create/edit/delete referenced by routes/batch.ts but undefined) fixed by hand
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:702-732 — user_has_permission joins a permissions row, so an undefined key is an inert predicate (10 such keys remain: ACM-P3-005)
findings.impact: The only defense against code/catalog drift remains manual review; a future undefined key silently produces an unsatisfiable guard (denial of service for non-bypass roles) or a dead RLS clause.
findings.recommendation: Add permission-catalog.test.ts parsing requirePermission("a","b") and RLS user_has_permission(_, 'a','b') strings and asserting membership in the migration catalog; run it in CI.

findings.title: Public route surface is broad and has no single documented inventory
evidence: docs/API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md:1-7 — explicitly marked 'Historical snapshot (2026-06-18) — not exhaustive'; defers to docs/openapi.yaml

public surface spans apps/api/src/routes/{auth,public,docs,health,webhooks}.ts plus inline blocks: file-requests.ts:75, status-page.ts:63, batch.ts, store/* public reads, store/quotes.ts:69 (public quote submit), analytics.ts:27, webhooks.ts:131/351/453/570
no docs section or CI guard enumerating/validating the anonymous surface

findings.recommendation: Generate a public-endpoints section from openapi.yaml (security: []) into docs, and add a test asserting every mutating route not on an allow-list is behind requireAuth.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: no single human-readable inventory; openapi.yaml marks public operations (partial mitigation) but the finding stands.

findings.title: `GET /roles/:id` and `GET /me/permissions` are readable without an admin gate
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/roles.ts:64 — GET /:id now requires requireAdmin
apps/api/src/routes/roles.ts:16 (GET /), :35 (GET /with-permissions), :218 (GET /:id/permissions) — requireAdmin
apps/api/src/routes/me.ts:18-31 — GET /me/permissions remains requireAuth-only and returns only the caller's own effective permissions (intended)

findings.title: RLS policies reference `manage` permissions that no role holds (dead predicates)
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:765,792 — user_has_permission(...,'documents','manage'); :1340,1381 'documents','upload'; :1350-1418 'documents','manage'
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:1160,1164 'tickets','manage'; :1185 'tickets','comment'; :1220-1295,1795-1910 'projects','manage'
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:1439 'contracts','create'; :1449,1489 'contracts','manage'; :1514 'appointments','schedule'; :1524,1528 'appointments','manage'; :1121,1125 'onboarding','update'

catalog scan of all 134 migrations (328 permission keys) — none of documents:manage, documents:upload, projects:manage, tickets:manage, tickets:comment, contracts:create, contracts:manage, appointments:schedule, appointments:manage, onboarding:update exist
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:702-732 — user_has_permission resolves only through a permissions row (role_permissions or user_permission_overrides), so these clauses can never be true
findings.impact: Inert clauses obscure the effective policy and mislead reviewers (e.g. can_read_document's documents:manage branch never fires; private/internal document visibility relies on uploaded_by/roles only). A future migration that adds one of these rows would silently widen the policies.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead clauses or add the intended permissions + grants deliberately; the catalog-lint test (ACM-P3-002) should cover RLS references so the set is machine-checked.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: 10 distinct RLS-referenced keys remain undefined in the catalog (documents:manage 22 refs, projects:manage 17 refs). Not a live exposure — the clauses are inert — but a correctness/review hazard.

findings.title: `profiles.is_super_admin` is user-writable under the RLS self-update policy (forgeable super-admin flag)
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:1015-1026 — policy profiles_update_self_or_super_admin USING/WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid() OR is_super_admin()); no column restriction
supabase/migrations/5302116_grant_table_privileges.sql:33-35 — blanket GRANT select,insert,update,delete on every public table to authenticated (only anon was revoked by 5302434:30-46)
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:638-650 — is_super_admin() reads profiles.is_super_admin for auth.uid() and is used by RLS policies and the API
apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts:62-75 — profile.is_super_admin grants every catalog permission and bypasses requirePermission entirely
supabase/migrations/5302026_...v3.sql:947-954 (organizations select), 997-1013 (profiles select), 1683-1690 (audit_logs select) — is_super_admin() alone grants all-tenant reads
no guard found: grep NEW.is_super_admin/OLD.is_super_admin and before-update triggers on profiles — only trg_profiles_updated_at (updated_at) exists
supabase/migrations/5302434:12-15 — the repo states 'There is no browser-to-PostgREST client in the repo', which is the only thing keeping the anon key out of client hands
findings.impact: Any authenticated user who can reach PostgREST with the project anon key (Supabase's standard public client credential; server-side-only in this repo today) can PATCH their own profiles row to is_super_admin=true. That yields every API permission (resolveEffectivePermissions bypass) and all-tenant RLS reads on policies whose super-admin branch is unscoped (organizations, profiles, audit_logs). The flag is the platform's highest-privilege identity attribute and it is not unforgeable.
findings.recommendation: Lock the column at the database: revoke UPDATE on public.profiles from authenticated (API writes use service role) or add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger raising unless current_user = 'service_role' when NEW.is_super_admin IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.is_super_admin; alternatively move the flag to a service-role-only table. Add a regression test that a user-scoped client cannot change the flag.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (not in the previous register; the extended check 'role and identity resolution relies on unforgeable attributes' fails here). Severity is P1 under the current server-only-anon-key architecture; treat as P0 if any direct Supabase client (mobile/browser) ships or the anon key becomes public.

findings.title: API-key `permissions` are decorative: keys act with the creator's full permissions and the column is never enforced
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302042_api_keys.sql:8 — permissions jsonb not null default '[]'
apps/api/src/middleware/api-key.ts:99 — authenticateApiKey returns normalizePermissions(data.permissions)
apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:70-75 — the value is attached to req.apiKey; grep of apps/api/src shows no consumer (req.apiKey.permissions is never read)
apps/api/src/middleware/api-key.ts:10-17 — documented design: the key acts as the creating user and the existing requireOrgAccess/requirePermission chain governs what it may do
apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:17-21 — the create schema (organizationId, name, expiresAt) cannot set permissions; :41 the list endpoint displays the (always empty) permissions column
findings.impact: Machine credentials cannot be least-privilege scoped: a key created by an org admin carries that admin's full role permissions in the key's org. Operators seeing an empty/permissions field may wrongly believe the key is restricted, and any future attempt to set permissions would have no effect.
findings.recommendation: Either enforce the intersection of the key's permissions with the creator's effective permissions in requirePermission (checking req.apiKey), or remove the column/display and document that API keys always act as their creator. Add a test for whichever contract is chosen.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d, discovered during the key-lifecycle verification (ACM-P2-006 family).

findings.title: `GET /api-keys` lists org keys for any org member (no `api-keys:view` gate)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:34-53 — GET / has no requirePermission (router-level requireAuth+requireOrgAccess only); returns name, key_prefix, permissions, expires_at, last_used_at, is_active
apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:56,94,146 — writes are correctly gated with api-keys:manage
supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql — the catalog defines api-keys:view, which is never consulted
findings.impact: Low-trust org members can enumerate machine-credential inventory (names, prefixes, expiry, last use), aiding targeting; prefixes are not secrets, so exposure is information disclosure only.
findings.recommendation: Add requirePermission('api-keys','view') to GET / or document the accepted posture (mirrors ACM-P2-005 for webhooks).
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; same pattern as the still-open webhook read gate (ACM-P2-005).

findings.title: AI copilot endpoints have no permission gate (any org member can run summarization and reply drafts)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:266-286 — GET /triage has no requirePermission
apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:289 — GET /copilot/:ticketId/summarize has no guard
apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:357 — POST /copilot/:ticketId/reply-draft has no guard; :361-372 loadOwned scopes the ticket to the caller's org
apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:174 — by contrast /triage/analyze is at least gated with ai:view; the catalog defines ai:view/create/edit/delete
findings.impact: Any approved org member, including read-only client roles, can invoke AI endpoints within their tenant (cost/abuse, inconsistent with the module's catalog); cross-tenant access is prevented by loadOwned.
findings.recommendation: Gate the copilot routes with requirePermission('ai','view') (reply-draft may warrant ai:create) or document the deliberate decision alongside the triage/analyze comment.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; same action-gating family as ACM-P2-004.

report:
# Access Control Matrix Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive (full hardening rerun)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: mainecybertech portal monorepo
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d` ("Merge PR #168: promote develop to main (metrics scrape fixes + register sync)")
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (prompt 24, area ACM)
- Area code: ACM
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/{run}/24_access_control_matrix_audit.md`
- Companion artifacts: role inventory, permission inventory, route access matrix and sensitive action matrix are embedded in this report (the run instructions limit this domain to two output files).
- Scope limitations:
  - Static review only: no hosted Supabase project, no running API, no database. RLS behavior under `auth.uid()` and the deployed `RLS_*_ENABLED` allow-list are `Unknown`/`not reproducible` from the repository alone.
  - The seeded catalog was read from migrations; the deployed catalog could differ (`Unknown`).
  - No changes to ACM-relevant files exist between the previous run's commit `9c0b88c` and `8d299b8d` (`git log 9c0b88c..8d299b8d -- <files>` is empty), so previous verifications were re-checked in place and re-bound to `8d299b8d`.

## Scope

Reviewed at `8d299b8d`:

- Roles: `apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts`, `apps/web/lib/roles.ts`, role catalog migrations (`5302026`, `5302128`).
- Permissions: `apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts`, `apps/api/src/middleware/permissions.ts`, catalog/grants migrations (`5302118`, `5302128`, `5302131`, `5302424`, `5302426`, `5302423`).
- Org/tenant/workspace membership: `middleware/org-access.ts`, `lib/tenant.ts`, `lib/admin-scope.ts`, `middleware/admin.ts`, `routes/memberships.ts`, `routes/organizations.ts`, `routes/users.ts`.
- Project/ticket/document/billing/API-key/webhook permission: all 60 files in `apps/api/src/routes/**` (442 route definitions) plus the 182 `requirePermission` call sites.
- Admin console: `routes/{admin,audit,analytics,business-os,dashboard,roles,users,bulk,search}.ts`; web `lib/auth/admin.ts`, `lib/auth/permissions.ts`, `components/{HasPermission,RouteGuard}.tsx`.
- Public/authenticated/internal routes: `apps/api/src/app.ts` mount table; `routes/{auth,public,docs,health,webhooks}.ts`; inline public blocks in `file-requests.ts`, `status-page.ts`, `batch.ts`, `store/*`, `analytics.ts`.
- Server actions / client-side hiding: `apps/web/app/(admin|portal)/**/actions.ts` sample; `apps/web/lib/auth/*`.
- API endpoints: route matrix (Appendix A).
- Background jobs: `apps/worker/src/tasks/*` identity model (service role, no user identity).
- DB helpers: `is_super_admin`, `is_org_member`, `is_org_approved_member`, `user_has_role`, `user_has_permission`, `can_read_document`, `approve_project_task`/`add_project_task_comment`.
- Middleware: `auth.ts`, `admin.ts`, `permissions.ts`, `org-access.ts`, `api-key.ts`, `entitlement.ts`, `csrf.ts`, `rate-limit.ts`.
- Audit logs: `services/audit.ts`, `services/impersonation.ts`, `routes/audit.ts`.
- Authz tests: `apps/api/src/__tests__` (133 files; 18 files assert 403/FORBIDDEN).

Not reviewed / out of scope: live RLS behavior, deployed env config, non-API clients (Terraform/CI covered by sibling domains), and the worker's task-level access control beyond its identity model.

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts` | Source | Trust tiers | `CROSS_TENANT_KEYS` (2) vs `ELEVATED_TENANT_KEYS` (6); `PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS` deprecated |
| `apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts` | Source | Effective permissions | `ADMIN_BYPASS_KEYS` (2); resolver with overrides; super-admin bypass at :62 |
| `apps/api/src/middleware/permissions.ts` | Source | Route enforcement | `requirePermission(module,action)`; org-scoped resolution; admin fallback |
| `apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts` | Source | Admin gate | Org-pinned admin semantics (ADMIN-P1-001 fix) |

## Executive Summary

The access-control system is materially sound at `8d299b8d`. Enforcement is data-driven and layered: 182 `requirePermission` call sites over 442 route definitions, an effective-permission resolver that unions approved-membership grants and per-org overrides, `requireOrgAccess` + `assertResourceOrg`/`loadOwned` for tenant scoping, a fail-closed RLS startup check, metered RLS bypass, and 18 test files asserting 403/FORBIDDEN behavior. The two headline problems from the previous run are closed: the client-onboarding router is fully permission-gated, and the cross-tenant trust set is now exactly `admin`/`super_admin` (elevated MSP roles no longer traverse tenants). `GET /roles/:id` is admin-gated, API-key expiry is enforced at authentication, and all 94 code-referenced permission keys exist in the catalog.

The remaining risk is concentrated in five places:

1. **A forgeable privilege flag (new, P1).** `profiles.is_super_admin` — the attribute that grants every API permission and unscoped all-tenant RLS reads — is writable by the `authenticated` role through the `profiles_update_self_or_super_admin` RLS policy (`5302026:1015-1026`) with no trigger or column guard. Direct PostgREST access requires the project anon key, which the repo keeps server-side (`5302434:12-15`), so today's exploitability is gated — but the attribute is not unforgeable, and the fix is a small migration.
2. **RLS is still opt-in per module (P2).** `getScopedClient` returns the service-role client unless the module is allow-listed; writes especially remain handler-scoped. Production now refuses to boot with an empty read list and bypass is metered, but the deployed allow-list is not verifiable from the repo.
3. **Read-side over-exposure (P2).** Webhook endpoint/delivery reads and the `api-keys` list are open to any org member; profiles are enumerable by email/id within a tenant; `ai.ts:174` still gates a write with `ai:view`; AI copilot routes are ungated.
4. **Secret/credential hygiene (P2).** Webhook signing secrets remain plaintext with no rotation/expiry; API keys have no pruner and their `permissions` column is decorative (keys act with the creator's full permissions).
5. **Model maintenance (P3).** No catalog-lint means 10 RLS-referenced keys (`documents:manage`, `projects:manage`, `tickets:comment`, …) are dead predicates; no single public-route inventory; no mutating-route guard-coverage gate.

Recommended order: lock `is_super_admin` at the DB (small, high value); then the read-gate fixes (webhooks, api-keys, profiles, AI routes); then catalog-lint (it would pass today and catch the RLS drift); continue the RLS write rollout.

## Findings

The full finding records (severity, evidence, impact, recommendation, owner, status, note) are in `_domains/24_access_control_matrix_audit.json`. Titles and outcomes:

1. **Client-onboarding mutations run without any `requirePermission` gate** — P1, `verified-fixed` (all routes gated; add a 403 regression test).
2. **`PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS` (org traversal) and `ADMIN_BYPASS_KEYS` (permission bypass) are inconsistent trust sets** — P2, `verified-fixed` (split at `roles.ts:27-37`; residual: no pinning test, deprecated constant still used for MSP-staff semantics in `tickets.ts`).
3. **RLS is not a database backstop on API requests (service-role is the default client)** — P2, `partially-fixed` (fail-closed boot + metering; writes/unlisted modules still service role; deployed allow-list unverifiable).
4. **Write and state-transition actions gated by `view` permissions (action mismatch)** — P2, `partially-fixed` (only `ai.ts:174` remains, documented in-code).
5. **Webhook endpoint and delivery reads are available to any org member (not manage-gated)** — P2, `still-open`.
6. **API keys store `expires_at` but nothing enforces or prunes expiry** — P2, `partially-fixed` (enforcement + tests present; no pruner).
7. **Webhook signing secrets are stored plaintext with no rotation or expiry** — P2, `still-open`.
8. **Profiles are enumerable by email/id for any authenticated user** — P2, `still-open` (RLS narrows to same-org; `select('*')` returns `encrypted_pii`).
9. **Client-side permission hiding is UI-only for several module actions** — P3, `partially-fixed` (API enforces broadly; no coverage gate).
10. **No catalog-lint: referenced permission keys are not checked against the `permissions` table** — P3, `still-open` (code-side drift currently zero).
11. **Public route surface is broad and has no single documented inventory** — P3, `still-open` (openapi marks 32 public ops).
12. **`GET /roles/:id` and `GET /me/permissions` are readable without an admin gate** — P3, `verified-fixed` (roles admin-gated; me self-scoped by design).
13. **RLS policies reference `manage` permissions that no role holds (dead predicates)** — P3, `still-open` (10 keys).
14. **`profiles.is_super_admin` is user-writable under the RLS self-update policy (forgeable super-admin flag)** — P1, `open` (new).
15. **API-key `permissions` are decorative: keys act with the creator's full permissions and the column is never enforced** — P2, `open` (new).
16. **`GET /api-keys` lists org keys for any org member (no `api-keys:view` gate)** — P3, `open` (new).
17. **AI copilot endpoints have no permission gate** — P3, `open` (new).
